name: PTN78000WAZT
title: PTN78000W / PTN78000H: 1.5 A wide-input adjustable step-down switching regulator module
summary: A 1.5 A non-isolated buck regulator module on a small double-sided board, set by one resistor. The PTN78000W runs from 7 V to 36 V and adjusts from 2.5 V to 12.6 V; the PTN78000H runs from 15 V to 36 V and adjusts from 11.85 V to 22 V. It switches at 550 kHz typical, reaches up to 95 % efficiency, and has an active-low inhibit input, undervoltage lockout, continuous current limit and thermal shutdown. It comes as a through-hole module (AH) or as a surface-mount module with tin-lead (AS) or lead-free (AZ) solder balls, rated -40 °C to 85 °C; the PTN78000WAZT is the W version, lead-free surface-mount, on tape and reel.
key_figures: 1.5 A (H: 1.5 A or 22.5 W, whichever is less)
7 V to 36 V (W); 15 V to 36 V (H)

notes: W in the name is the 2.5 V to 12.6 V output version (7 V to 36 V input); H is the 11.85 V to 22 V output version (15 V to 36 V input).

The suffix after the letter gives the pin style: AH is the horizontal through-hole module (EUS package), AS the horizontal surface-mount module with tin-lead solder balls, and AZ the horizontal surface-mount module with lead-free (SnAgCu) solder balls (both EUT package). A trailing T is tape and reel of 250.
All of these parts are active and in production.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Common return for both the input and the output power paths, and the 0 V level that the Inhibit and VO Adjust controls are measured from.

pins.name: VI
pins.function: Positive input supply, measured against GND.

pins.name: Inhibit
pins.function: Active-low on/off control referred to GND, meant to be pulled down by an open-collector or open-drain switch. Pulled low, it shuts the output off and the input draw falls to the standby current. Left open, the module runs whenever a valid input is present (internal pull-up, about 1.5 V open-circuit).

pins.name: VO Adjust
pins.function: Output set-point. A 1 % resistor with 100 ppm/°C or better stability, RSET, goes from this pin to GND (pin 1). With the pin open the output sits at the bottom of its adjust range. Set-point range: 2.5 V to 12.6 V (PTN78000W), 11.85 V to 22 V (PTN78000H).

pins.name: VO
pins.function: Regulated positive output, measured against GND.

circuits.title: Standard application
circuits.description: The minimum circuit for either version. A ceramic capacitor sits across the input, a 100 µF electrolytic across the output, and RSET from VO Adjust to GND picks the output voltage. The Inhibit line is brought out as a terminal; left unconnected the module simply runs.

parts.value: per Table 2 or the RSET equation
parts.note: 0.05 W, 1 %, required above 2.5 V (W) or 11.824 V (H)

circuits.title: PTN78000W VO Adjust resistor placement
circuits.description: The set-point resistor goes straight from pin 4 to pin 1 on traces of its own, as near the module as it will fit. A 2.2 µF ceramic capacitor bypasses the input and 100 µF the output. Nothing capacitive may be hung on VO Adjust, to GND or to VO, since it upsets the loop.

circuits.title: On/off inhibit control circuit
circuits.description: A 12 V to 5 V PTN78000W stage switched by a BSS138. With Q1 on, pin 3 is held at GND and the output is off, the input drawing about 17 mA. Turning Q1 off releases pin 3 and the module soft-starts, reaching regulation within 20 ms. RSET of 21 kΩ sets 5 V; the load is resistive, 1.5 A in the test.

circuits.title: Adding high-frequency bypass capacitors to the input and output
circuits.description: Extra ceramic capacitors for lower ripple and noise. C2 is the required input ceramic and C1 a second 2.2 µF ceramic on the input; C3 is the required 100 µF output capacitor, which helps transient response, and C4 is a ceramic at the output terminals that trims the output ripple. Inhibit is left open.

circuits.title: Adding π filters (IO ≤ 3 A)
circuits.description: A π filter on each side of the module: L1, a ferrite bead or a 1 µH to 5 µH inductor, sits between the input terminal and VI with ceramics C1 and C2 on either side of it; L2 does the same at the output between C3 and the C4/C5 pair. With ceramic capacitors the filter cuts ripple and noise by 20 dB or more. Inhibit is left open.

where.VMIN: bottom of the adjust range: 2.5 V (PTN780x0W), 11.824 V (PTN780x0H)

operation.text: A step-down integrated switching regulator module on a double-sided, case-less board, the third generation of the 78ST100 line and a replacement for the 78ST100, PT78ST100, PT5100 and PT6100 single-in-line products. It delivers up to 1.5 A and suits general loads running from 12 V, 24 V or 28 V DC buses. The W version adjusts from 2.5 V to 12.6 V and can run with as little as 2 V headroom (7 V in for 5 V out); the H version adjusts from 11.85 V to 22 V with 3 V headroom (15 V in for 12 V out). Efficiency reaches 95 %.

One resistor from VO Adjust (pin 4) to GND (pin 1) sets the output. Open, the output stays at its lowest value (2.5 V for W, 11.85 V for H). Table 2 gives standard values with the output each really gives, Tables 3 and 4 list a value for each step of output, and the RSET equation covers any other output. A 0.05 W, 1 % resistor of 100 ppm/°C or better is adequate.

operation.topic: Input voltage headroom and duty cycle
operation.text: As a buck regulator the module needs the input to stay a minimum margin above the output to keep regulating. The internal PWM also has a smallest workable duty cycle, which sets the largest usable ratio of input to output voltage. The input limits per version are in the equations; Table 2 gives the input range for each common output, and the electrical tables give the adjust range for each input band.

At least 2.2 µF of ceramic capacitance, X5R or X7R, within 0.5 inch (1.27 cm) of the input pins. Electrolytics may be added but never replace the ceramic; any nonceramic input capacitor needs a ripple-current rating of at least 650 mA rms, a need that more ceramic capacitance reduces. Tantalum capacitors are not recommended on the input: none was found that meets the usual 2 × (maximum DC voltage + AC ripple) derating. Polymer tantalum parts, typically rated 20 V, may be used for inputs up to 16 V.

At least 2 × 4.7 µF of ceramic capacitance, X5R or X7R, within 0.5 inch (1.27 cm) of the input pins. Electrolytics may be added but never replace the ceramic; any nonceramic input capacitor needs a ripple-current rating of at least 350 mA rms. The same limits on tantalum and polymer tantalum apply as for the W version.

At least 100 µF is needed for stability, ceramic or electrolytic, placed near the output pins; a nonceramic part needs at least 150 mA rms ripple rating, and a good computer-grade electrolytic is adequate. A ceramic capacitor may also be fitted no more than 0.5 inch (1.27 cm) from the output pin. Where the load steps, more electrolytic capacitance near the load improves the response; it decouples over about 2 kHz to 150 kHz. Aluminium electrolytics suit ambients above 0 °C; below 0 °C use tantalum or OS-CON types. With nonceramic capacitors the combined ESR must not fall below 10 mΩ (17 mΩ when using a capacitor's maximum ESR figure). Ceramic capacitors at the output have a combined ESR that is not critical while their total stays at or below 200 µF.

Above about 150 kHz aluminium electrolytics lose effect, so multilayer ceramics are added to cut reflected input ripple or improve transient response; they have low ESR and resonate above the regulator's bandwidth. On the output, tantalum capacitors suit ambients below 0 °C; AVX TPS, Sprague 593D/594/595 and Kemet T495/T510/T520 are preferred for their surge, dissipation and ripple ratings. General-purpose tantalums with higher ESR and lower ripple and surge ratings are less reliable, and parts with no stated ESR or surge rating should not be used for power. With OS-CON and polymer tantalum outputs, the minimum-ESR limit is reached before the maximum capacitance. Ripple-current rating and ESR at 100 kHz are the figures that matter for performance and capacitor life.

Transient response is specified for a 1 A/µs load step with the required output capacitance. Faster steps, beyond the loop's bandwidth, are met only by the output decoupling, so a tighter deviation or higher di/dt calls for more output capacitance chosen for type, value and ESR.

Built as in the standard application, the module regulates as soon as a valid input appears. Internal soft-start slows the rise of the output to limit inrush, adding a delay of typically 5 ms to 10 ms from the moment the input is recognised as valid.

The module stays off until the input passes the UVLO threshold, so it does not draw heavy current from a source that is still coming up. Thresholds: 5.5 V rising and 5.2 V falling (W), 12.2 V rising and 12 V falling (H).

The current limit is continuous: an overload cannot draw more than the limit, and the output voltage falls as the load tries to take more. Current keeps flowing into the fault until it clears, then the output recovers at once. Sustained limiting heats the module, and if it gets hot enough the overtemperature protection starts switching the output fully off at intervals.

If the internal control IC's junction gets too hot (from lost airflow, high ambient or a long current-limit spell), the module turns off and the output drops to zero; it restarts by itself once it has cooled a few degrees. This is a last-resort safeguard, not a substitute for staying inside the derating curves: running above them, even below the shutdown point, shortens the module's life.

With pin 3 open the module runs whenever a valid input is applied. Pulling pin 3 low through a switch such as Q1 turns the output off; the output then decays as the load drains the capacitors, and the input draws typically 17 mA. Releasing pin 3 starts a soft-start power-up, with the output in regulation within 20 ms.

The module already has ceramic capacitors inside at input and output. A single 1 µF ceramic across the output terminals (C4) lowers output ripple and noise by 10 % to 30 % for modules rated under 3 A; C3 is there for transient response and does not reduce ripple. The module draws input current in pulses at its switching frequency, so the reflected input ripple scales with the source impedance, wiring included; a ceramic of at least 1 µF (C1) near the input pins lowers it by 30 % to 50 %.

For more reduction, a ferrite bead (Fair-Rite 2673000701 or equivalent, 12.5 mm × 3 mm, low DC resistance) placed in series in the input or the output line, with ceramic capacitors on each side, forms a π filter that lowers ripple and noise by at least 20 dB, with its rejection at the switching frequency (650 kHz to 1 MHz). It must sit as close as possible to the module's input or output pins. A surface-mount bead, Fair-Rite 2773021447, is also made; the through-hole bead is rated 5 A and works up to 5 A on the output bus. A 1 µH to 5 µH inductor can take the place of the bead.

The derating curves give the ambient at which the internal parts stay at or below their makers' temperature limits, for the module soldered to a 100 mm × 100 mm double-sided board with 2 oz copper. Surface-mount versions need several plated vias around the power pins to carry heat away.
ESD protection is limited: keep the leads shorted together or the module in conductive foam while it is stored or handled, to protect the MOS gates.

Put RSET right next to the regulator, wired straight between pins 4 and 1 on dedicated traces, and never fit a capacitor between VO Adjust and either GND or VO. Input ceramics go within 0.5 inch (1.27 cm) of the input pins. On the surface-mount EUT version each input, ground and output pin connects to the inner power plane through two or more vias of 0.025 inch (0.63 mm) inside diameter, or the equivalent.
